phrases.text: The speed of the boat in still water is fifteen kilometer per hour,
and the speed of the stream is
We need to find the total time taken for the whole journey.
let us quickly recall one basic concept. The boat's speed in still water means the speed when there is no current.
The stream helps the boat while moving downstream,
and the stream slows down the boat while moving upstream, so the speeds get subtracted.
This is the main idea of the question. So first, let us find both speeds.
Downstream speed equals speed of boat plus stream speed, which is fifteen plus three equals eighteen kilometer per hour.
Upstream speed equals speed of boat minus stream speed, which is fifteen minus three
The formula we need is time equals distance divided by speed.
Now that we have the speeds,
Time taken downstream equals thirty-six divided by eighteen equals two hours.

Time taken upstream equals thirty-six divided by twelve equals three hours. Now only one step is left. The total time is two plus three equals five hours. So the final answer is five hours, which is option C.
